newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka slashes turnover tax on selected items.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka slashes turnover tax on selected items.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Monday it was exempting selected items from turnover tax and halving the levy on some businesses with immediate effect.
"It is all to do with harmonising taxes to make way for administrative ease and taxpayer convenience," a Treasury official told Reuters.
The items exempted from turnover tax are computers, monitors and accessories, cotton yarn used in the handloom industry and certain beverage cartons.
These items were previously taxed at between 10 and 20 percent.
Businesses exempt from the tax include those which convert grey cloth to finished fabric and those that add value to garments by chemical washing or dyeing.
These business earlier paid a turnover tax of 7.0 percent.
Turnover tax levied on financiers or money lenders, other than banks and pawnbrokers, has been reduced to 2.0 percent from 4.0 percent.
Sri Lanka eventually aims to introduce a goods and services tax, but it was not immediately clear when the new system would be implemented.
